question.latex: The equation of motion of a particle is given by $x = a \sin\left$50t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right$\text{ cm}$. The particle will come to rest at time $t_1$ and it will have zero acceleration at time $t_2$. The $t_1$ and $t_2$ respectively are _______.
question.unicode: The equation of motion of a particle is given by x = a sinleft50t + (π/3)righttext{ cm}. The particle will come to rest at time t_1 and it will have zero acceleration at time t_2. The t_1 and t_2 respectively are _______.
question.plainText: The equation of motion of a particle is given by x = a sinleft50t + (pi)/(3)righttext{ cm}. The particle will come to rest at time t_1 and it will have zero acceleration at time t_2. The t_1 and t_2 respectively are _______.

explanation.latex:
Velocity $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 50a \cos\left(50t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$. For particle to come to rest, $v=0 \implies 50t_1 + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies 50t_1 = \frac{\pi}{6} \implies t_1 = \frac{\pi}{300}\text{ s}$.
Acceleration $A = \frac{dv}{dt} = -2500a \sin\left(50t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$. For zero acceleration, $A=0 \implies 50t_2 + \frac{\pi}{3} = \pi \implies 50t_2 = \frac{2\pi}{3} \implies t_2 = \frac{2\pi}{150} = \frac{\pi}{75}\text{ s}$.
explanation.unicode:
Velocity v = (dx/dt) = 50a cosleft(50t + (π/3)right). For particle to come to rest, v=0 implies 50t_1 + (π/3) = (π/2) implies 50t_1 = (π/6) implies t_1 = (π/300)text{ s}.
Acceleration A = (dv/dt) = -2500a sinleft(50t + (π/3)right). For zero acceleration, A=0 implies 50t_2 + (π/3) = π implies 50t_2 = (2π/3) implies t_2 = (2π/150) = (π/75)text{ s}.
